brief: A seven-cell honeycomb standing on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet.

requirements.evidence: 7 full bases (pieces) at 0,0 and its six neighbours, held together with 12 joint bolts

requirements.requirement: Stands on at least three stud spikes facing down as feet
requirements.evidence: 6 stud spikes facing down at the six points where three cells meet around the centre cell

finish.summary: I built a seven-cell honeycomb from full bases: a centre cell at 0,0 with all six neighbouring cells around it. It stands on six stud spikes facing down, one at each point where three cells meet around the centre, so they ring it evenly. I also ran the two standard finishing steps: every open outer face has a solid end cap (18 caps), and 12 joint bolts lock the cells together. That makes 31 parts, and the print estimate is about 2.3 kg of filament and 3,775 minutes of printing. The final check found no rule problems and no parts colliding.

lines.label: M6 brass heat-set insert, 7.6 mm (initeq M6-1.0 Short)
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
